semantics: src/ is not modified, no flag is added and the fingerprint does not change. Every match is the C2 mirror match (buildChallengeMatchSetup -> the ladder ladderSetup -> mirrorSetup -> assembleMatch -> the runChallenge tick loop; the functions are copied verbatim from measure_challenge_c2_3aB.mjs and V1 checks them record by record). The only intervention: after assembleMatch and before the first tick, the engine hero list e.players is reordered IN PLACE so the five red heroes come first (b-order within a side unchanged). The engine iterates this.players for every per-hero step (casting loop, passives, attacks, kill resolution); it keeps no cached sub-list of players and splits teams by p.side, not by index (code audit, round-2 doc section 2.1); spawn positions (rng) and the tie-break hash (construction index) are fixed in the constructor, before the reorder
background: C2 (be02333f): in true mirrors (both sides the same team, heroes, mastery, stats and tactic; STANDARD layout) switching the skill layer on (L1 -> L3a, which also switches the live assembly order) moved the blue win rate by +6.9 pp pooled (2.9..10.8, z 3.40, SKILL_LAYER_SIDE_EFFECT), concentrated in topheavyDef (+16.0; mirror +3.8, rotation +0.8, balancedDef +6.8 NONE). The code audit found no side branch in the skill rules; candidate sources: (a) the hero processing order (blue first in this.players: same-tick mutual kills resolved blue first, kill XP lost by the second killer, passives, displacement), (b) the systems heroSkillsOn switches on (per-pit approach geometry), (c) the live assembly order. In the ladder (real, non-mirror pairings) the STANDARD skills step was +0.1 only, so the mirror effect is not a general challenge effect

questions.Q1: primary: does reversing the hero processing order reverse the skill-layer side effect? On the same fresh seeds, per seed: dB = W_B(L3a) - W_B(L1) (blue first), dR = W_R(L3a) - W_R(L1) (red first); order component O = (dB - dR)/2, position component P = (dB + dR)/2 (what stays with blue when the order is reversed); per lineup and pooled. Review D5 #1: blue-first is re-run on the fresh seeds, so O + P is not fixed in advance by the selected C2 value
questions.Q2: secondary (descriptive): the first-mover advantage per context A = (W_B - W_R)/2 at L1 (no skills: basic attacks, minion / tower fights) and at L3a
questions.Q3: secondary (descriptive): the live assembly order alone (L1 -> L1o, blue first) and the skills-only step (L1o -> L3a), per lineup and pooled
questions.Q0: replication (descriptive): the blue-first skill step dB on the fresh seeds next to the C2 value (+6.9 pooled, selected for significance)

analysis.labels: MATERIAL at |z| >= 2.81 (review D5 #6: O and P x (4 lineups + pooled) = 10 tests, Bonferroni 0.05 / 10), HINT if the unadjusted 95% interval excludes 0, else NONE; every NONE / HINT is reported with MDE = (2.81 + 0.84) x se
analysis.verdict: on the pooled O and P: ORDER_DRIVEN if O is MATERIAL and P is not; POSITION_DRIVEN if P is MATERIAL and O is not; MIXED if both; LINEUP_SPECIFIC if neither pooled value is but a lineup O or P is; else INCONCLUSIVE. The verdict is null (at most INCONCLUSIVE) if any match errored; INSTRUMENT (no result file) if the live check failed, V1 failed (including a missing C2 record) or the error rule says STOP
analysis.prediction: if the +6.9 pp is entirely the hero processing order, dR is about -dB, so O is about +6.9 and P about 0 (ORDER_DRIVEN); if it is entirely per-side geometry or another blue-fixed loop, dR is about dB, O about 0 and P about +6.9 (POSITION_DRIVEN)
analysis.power: per-match sd of a paired step difference about 0.70 (C2); O and P each average two independent steps: se about 0.70 x sqrt(2) / 2 / sqrt(1200) = 1.43 pp pooled, MDE about 5.2 pp at |z| 2.81 and 80% power; per lineup about 10.4 pp. If the fresh dB is much smaller than the C2 +6.9 (winner's curse), O and P will usually be INCONCLUSIVE; that outcome is reported as such, not as evidence of no effect
analysis.interpretation: what a verdict means for an engine change (the Owner decides; the study only measures). Review D5 #5: O measures the order x skills interaction (the first-mover advantage at L3a minus that at L1), not the effect of any particular fix. ORDER_DRIVEN => the mirror skill-step effect depends on the hero processing order; an order fix (simultaneous resolution or alternating first mover) is a candidate that must be designed and measured separately, and this study does not bound what it would change; POSITION_DRIVEN => reversing the hero order does not move the effect: the source is per-side geometry or one of the blue-fixed structures that this study does not reverse (see limitations), so an order fix of the hero loop alone is not supported; MIXED => both; INCONCLUSIVE / LINEUP_SPECIFIC => no engine change is supported by this study. In every case the ladder result (STANDARD skills step +0.1 in real pairings) limits how much of the real challenge side bias a mirror finding explains; the challenge side-bias STOP stays
analysis.secondary: Q2 first-mover advantage A = (W_B - W_R)/2 at L1 and L3a; Q3 assembly order (L1 -> L1o, blue first) and skills only (L1o -> L3a, blue first) on the fresh seeds; descriptive, same labels

errors: errored matches are never retried; the tool applies errorRule (studyRunner): more than 1% errored => STOP(INSTRUMENT), no result file; any error => verdict null, outcome INCONCLUSIVE (review D5 #3)
limitations: only the hero list order is reversed; at least these blue-fixed structures are not (review D5 #4): the loops over the fixed list ["blue", "red"] in LogicEngine.js (lines 129, 233, 249, 412, 1029, 3241, 6081, 6378, 7249, 7439), the tuple loops at 5437 and 5828, the paired calls at 5973-5974 (advance) and 6038-6039 (strike), the id tie-breaks by localeCompare (about 14 sites, e.g. 4483 [...b, ...r] sorted by id, which favour b*), the Object.entries order of the towers and the minion lists. P can therefore still contain order effects from those structures, and POSITION_DRIVEN does not mean "geometry only"
random draws are consumed in hero order, so the reorder also changes which hero gets which draw; in a mirror this is symmetric noise, not a bias
